rundown: Phoenix beat V-Hawks 66-46 at Resch Center in Ashwaubenon, WI in front of 3,034. Phoenix led 24-23 at half-time and never looked back. By ESPN's win probability it was never really in doubt (never below 98%).
Leading the way — V-Hawks: Treyton Fletcher 11 pts, 6 reb; Landon Thousand 6 ast. Phoenix: LeBron Thomas 14 pts, 7 reb; Marcus Hall 5 ast.
Where Phoenix won it: they shot 37% to 31%, won the boards 42-32 and turned it over 12 times to 19.

review.title: The algo's call
review.body:
Logged before the start, last snapshot Nov 13, 11:58 AM ET. It had V-Hawks 45% and Phoenix 55%, projecting V-Hawks 79.6 – Phoenix 80.8 (160.4 total, Phoenix by 1.3).

Final: V-Hawks 46 – Phoenix 66. Right winner: it had Phoenix at 55%.

Thin data: 3 of 6 key inputs were sourced (missing: VTBO pts scored, VTBO pts allowed, VTBO lineup rating or past seasons), so league averages filled the gaps. It was logged as a no-data call: graded and learned from, never offered as a bet.

review.title: How the ratings held up
review.body:
V-Hawks came in with a league-average attack and a league-average defense (no scoring on file: rated at the league average), worth about 14 and 14 games of evidence. Projected to score 79.6, they scored 46 (−33.6 points, 42% under); projected to allow 80.8, they allowed 66 (−14.8 points, 18% under).

Phoenix came in with a league-average attack and a 3% leakier than average defense (2-2, 77.5 scored and 72 allowed a game over 4 games), worth about 176 and 178 games of evidence. Projected to score 80.8, they scored 66 (−14.8 points, 18% under); projected to allow 79.6, they allowed 46 (−33.6 points, 42% under).

The bigger miss was V-Hawks' scoring (-33.6 points against projection); both sides underscored their projections, so the game ran colder than either team's numbers said.

review.title: Where the result sat in the simulations
review.body:
Total: 112 against 160.4 projected (-48.4), about the 1st percentile of the simulated totals (a typical game swings ±14.5).

Margin: Phoenix by 20 against Phoenix by 1.3 projected, about the 96th percentile of the simulated margins (typical swing ±11).

An outlier: the simulations had a result this far off less than about 5% of the time, which usually means an input was wrong or missing, not just bad luck.

review.title: Situational factors, checked
review.body: Nothing situational moved this projection (rest, travel, form and conditions were all normal), so it came down to team strength.

review.title: Against the market
review.body: No line was priced for this game (no posted odds, or not enough data to price one).

review.title: What could have made it wrong
review.body:
Flagged going in: early-season numbers were thin; inputs were missing (VTBO pts scored, VTBO pts allowed, VTBO lineup rating or past seasons); there were no odds to check the projection against.

The projection missed by a lot, so those flags likely mattered here.

review.title: What the algo learns
review.body:
This game's own lesson: scoring came in at ×0.697 of the raw projection, and the home side beat its projected margin by +19.8 points. It counts toward CBB scoring level, home edge and both teams' attack and defense corrections (it's how teams with no standings on the routes build a record of their own).

Across 434 graded CBB games the algo now scales scoring ×0.996 and gives home teams +1.1 points. Team corrections so far: Phoenix attack ×0.986, defense ×0.968 (4 games).

review.title: Bottom line
review.body: Right side, total outside its normal range, margin outside its normal range (off by 18.7 points), no bet.
